scores.reason: Situation = non-diabetic adults with documented hypoglycaemia who get the insulin/C-peptide/proinsulin/BOHB work-up. No US count of such work-ups was found. Chain: insulinoma incidence 4 per million per year (Olmsted County, 1991) x about 340 million US residents = about 1,360 new insulinomas per year; insulinoma was 13% of 92 adults (tertiary cohort, supervised fast) and 6% of 70 admitted adults (single endocrinology department), so about 10,000 to 23,000 adults evaluated per year if those yields apply (point estimate about 15,000). The yield shares come from two single-centre cohorts and are assumptions for the US (clarification 21). Range 5,000 to over 100,000. Measure type: fasting/spontaneous-hypoglycaemia insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin (secretion measures, not an IR index).

scores.reason: Endocrine Society 2009 guideline Recommendation 2.1 (1, moderate quality) recommends, in adults with hypoglycaemia without diabetes and no evident cause, measuring plasma glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate during spontaneous hypoglycaemia (with sulfonylurea screen and glucagon response), compared with a much less thorough work-up; Rec 1.1 limits work-up to documented Whipple's triad. ENETS 2016 restates the thresholds. It is a graded recommendation, not a statement that the test must precede the decision, so 3 not 4 (clarifications 7, 13). The guideline is from 2009; no newer Endocrine Society version was found in the screened records. Measure type: spontaneous or fasting-induced hypoglycaemia sampling (secretion measures).

scores.reason: Situation = children aged 8 to 17 years within 8 weeks of Stage 3 T1D diagnosis who have at least one islet autoantibody and are screened by peak C-peptide for teplizumab. Chain: about 18,300 new T1D cases per year under age 20 (SEARCH-based estimate for 2014 to 2015; 2017 to 2018 incidence 22.2 per 100,000, rising about 2% per year, so about 19,000 now, assumption); age share 8 to 17 about 60% (derived from SEARCH 2017 to 2018 counts 179, 341, 445, 194 for ages 0-4, 5-9, 10-14, 15-19, prorating ages 8-9 and 15-17; derivation is mine) = about 11,000; times at least one autoantibody about 90% (assumption, range 85 to 95%) = about 10,000 to 10,300. Range 8,500 to 12,500 crosses the 10,000 boundary, so bin 3 or 2, low confidence. I score 3 (point estimate above 10,000 after growth); the alternative is bin 2 if incidence is flat at the 2014-2015 level or antibody-positive share is under about 91%. Count is patients in whom the question arises, not those who pass the 0.2 pmol/mL cut or are treated. Measure type: mixed-meal-stimulated C-peptide.

scores.reason: Situation = adults with suspected insulinoma and a negative supervised fast whose symptoms are postprandial, who need an OGTT- or meal-based insulin/glucose test. Postprandial-only presentation was 6% of 237 surgically confirmed insulinomas at Mayo and up to 18% in the ENETS-cited single-centre series, so about 80 to 245 insulinomas per year. The number tested is higher: insulinoma was 13% of 92 non-diabetic adults with a fast (reactive hypoglycaemia 87%); assuming insulinoma is about 5% (range 1 to 10%) of those tested with a negative fast and postprandial symptoms gives about 1,600 (range 800 to 5,000). The yield is an assumption. Alternative bin 1 if yield is above about 8% (under 1,000 tested), bin 3 if yield is under about 0.8%. Measure type: post-load (OGTT) or mixed-meal insulin and glucose.

scores.reason: Situation = children and adolescents with diabetes for over about 2 years labelled T1D in whom a non-T1D type (MODY, T2D) is suspected and C-peptide is measured. scores.reason: Two guideline texts were read. ADA Standards of Care 2026 section 2, Figure 2.1 footnotes: a C-peptide test is indicated only in people on insulin; a random sample within 5 hours of eating can replace a stimulation test; at or above 600 pmol/L the circumstances do not matter; values 200 to 600 pmol/L are usually consistent with T1D or MODY. National criteria from the UK are not counted (clarification 6). Alternative 3 if ADA text is read as covering youth.

anchor_issues: Rows 1, 2, 23, 24 (D7): clarification 4 says count patients in whom the question arises (all worked up), but no source for the size of the work-up population exists; I used a back-calculation from insulinoma incidence divided by single-centre yield. Clarification 24 says not to switch to the broader count; I did not, and gave the alternative in the reason.

Row 24 (D7): the row text defines the situation as 'new hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia', which is a diagnosis-level count, while clarification 4 asks for the work-up-level count. I scored the row text and put the broader count in the note.

Row 29 (D7): point estimate sits on the 10,000 boundary between bin 2 and 3; clarification 3 gives no tie rule beyond 'bin containing the point estimate'. I used a growth-adjusted estimate (above 10,000) and recorded bin 2 as the alternative.

Row 29 (D3): clarification 7 says 4 when the label requires the test for the decision. The label says to select 'based on confirmation' of C-peptide at or above 0.2 pmol/mL but allows an alternative method of measuring peak C-peptide, so the analyte is required and the protocol is not. I scored 4.

Row 1 and 2 (D3): the Endocrine Society recommendation is graded 1 and phrased as a recommended strategy versus a less thorough work-up, not as a mandatory step. Clarification 13 (4 only if the test must be done before the decision) puts it at 3; a reader could argue 4 for the supervised-fast panel.
Row 22 (D3): the test is a procedure with insulin as the readout, not a stand-alone insulin measurement; I scored the guideline status of the procedure as the measurement context.

Row 33 (D3): the ADA algorithm footnote is in a figure, not a numbered recommendation, and does not name youth; clarification 14 does not say how to score figure footnotes. I scored 2 and gave 3 as the alternative.
Row 23 (D3): the row names the OGTT; the Endocrine Society text names a mixed-meal test. The anchor does not say whether a close alternative stimulus counts, so I treated it as not the same test.

Share of US youth with T1D label crossing into a suspected non-T1D evaluation each year set to 25% of the antibody-negative pool; share of new T1D cases that are autoantibody-positive set to 90% (no US source retrieved).

Setting tags assume the work-up is ordered by endocrinology (specialist outpatient) although the critical sample is often drawn in the ED or inpatient; the sampling procedure for row 22 is inpatient or procedural.
